name: Pomegranates
tile_uses: Over squash, salads, yogurt, the drink
why_now: California grows nearly all of the country's pomegranates, and the harvest runs from late September into November. In October they're heavy, cheap by the piece, and sold everywhere from the farmers market to the corner store. By spring, the only ones left are imported.
how_to_choose: Heavy for its size — weight is juice
Angular and a little lopsided, with flat faces; round ones aren't full yet
A small dry crack is fine; a soft or damp spot is not
buy_this_much: 3. One pomegranate gives about a cup of seeds, which is a week of scattering.
price_note: Priced by the piece, so the heaviest one in the bin is the best deal.

flavor_paths.name: Scattered
flavor_paths.description: Over anything roasted, rich, or beige. The default.

flavor_paths.name: In the salad
flavor_paths.description: With arugula and dates. The weekend.

flavor_paths.name: Pressed
flavor_paths.description: Juiced through a strainer, into the jamaica.

weekday_uses: Over roasted kabocha while it's hot
On sweet potato tacos in place of salsa
In the rice bowl, for the crunch
weekend_use: Half a pomegranate's seeds in the October salad, next to the whole fish.
storage: Whole, in the fridge for a month or more. Seeded, five days in a covered container.
one_thing_to_learn: To seed one without a mess, score around the crown, pull the fruit apart into sections, and work the seeds loose in a bowl of water. The seeds sink and the white pith floats. Skim, drain, done.
market_question: Which ones came off the tree most recently?
